note: CPU-first measurements on the user's Mac (decision CF3a): Apple M4 Pro (10 performance + 4 efficiency cores), 48 GB, macOS; turing-cpu built from feat/cpu-first-inference (libllama 171527522, KleidiAI, Metal off), 10 threads, repack off. gpt-oss-120b MXFP4 (63.4 GB, bigger than RAM) from the internal SSD and from a SanDisk Extreme Pro 55AF on USB (link 10 Gb/s). Other apps were open: about 20-26 GB of RAM was left for the model (turing-cpu's peak resident size 26 GB); the memory state before and after each run is logged.

drive_read_GB_s.note: scratchpad readspeed.py: F_NOCACHE reads; seq_8m = one thread, 8 MB in order; rand_1m_tN = N threads, 1 MB at random 1 MB-aligned offsets over the file.

decode_gpt_oss_120b.note: turing-cpu bench --threads 10 --prompt-tokens 64 --gen-tokens 64 --reps 2 --no-repack [--readahead]: median of 2 after a 16-token warm-up, as Wave 2 ran it. No drop_caches on macOS without sudo: before each run the other drive's copy was read through the page cache (flush_s). Model load read the whole file (load_s). Read-ahead was slower than plain mmap from both drives here, where on Linux (Wave 2, 28 GB cache) it was 3.8x faster.
decode_gpt_oss_120b.thermal: The drive's temperature was not monitored; the SanDisk rows ran 5-15 minutes into sustained reads and may already be throttled.

verify_k_tokens_cached.note: scratchpad verify.py: one eval of the next k true tokens (all logits) at 16 positions, k rotated, cache truncated back after each. The k windows overlapped, so the experts were already in RAM (gb_read 0): this is the in-memory cost of checking k drafts, not the drive-bound one it set out to measure. distinct_experts and gb_wanted (read-ahead's counters, summed over the 36 MoE layers) show the experts k tokens choose: 144 for one token (4 a layer), 634 for eight.

speculation_gpt_oss_120b.note: scratchpad spec.sh: turing-cpu generate, Wave 3's code-edit prompt in gpt-oss's format (final channel), 200 greedy tokens, prompt-lookup drafts 0 and 4 alternated twice per drive, plain mmap, repack off; seconds include the prompt.
text_identical: internal: d4 text identical to d0
speculation_gpt_oss_120b.stopped: Stopped after the first two SanDisk runs: the user reported the drive overheating, after about 40 minutes in which it served ~0.5 TB of reads at up to 1 GB/s (the copy, cache flushes, and each run's load reading the whole 63 GB file). Their 1.0 tok/s, against 10.7 in decode_gpt_oss_120b, is taken as thermal throttling: not a measurement of speculation. Internal-SSD runs not done.
speculation_gpt_oss_120b.finding: Internal SSD: 2.0 tok/s with and without drafts (prompt included). Prompt lookup drafted 14 tokens and 7 were accepted in 108: the type-hinted answer rarely repeats the original's token runs, so this prompt cannot show whether speculation pays more when the drive is the limit.

bench_vs_real_text.note: scratchpad mixcheck.py, internal SSD, one process: 64 tokens of real greedy decoding of a fresh prompt alternated with 64 one-token evals of random token ids (as turing-cpu bench and llama-bench decode), twice. Read-ahead only counted (a window it never completes): the chosen experts' bytes and the share not in the page cache (mincore). bench_recheck: the same turing-cpu bench as decode_gpt_oss_120b, run again after these.
bench_vs_real_text.finding: Real text misses about twice the expert bytes of random ids (11.8-14.2% against 6.1-6.9% of 1.9 GB a token) and decodes at 3.4-4.1 tok/s against 5.7-6.1; bench, whose warm-up and 64-token prompt are random ids too, reports 16.2-17.3. For an MoE bigger than RAM, bench overstates real-text decode about 4x on this Mac. Wave 2's numbers (results_cpu_waves123_c4a / waves23_c4a) were measured the same way.

real_text_readahead_vs_mmap.note: scratchpad realtext.py / realtext.sh, internal SSD only: gpt-oss-120b real greedy decoding, 64 tokens after each of 28 different prompts (4 per process, no prompt reused, so no process inherits another's experts), processes in the order mmap(count-only), readahead, readahead, mmap(count-only), plain, readahead, plain. plain = mmap with nothing else; mmap = mmap with read-ahead only counting missing bytes (mincore), which itself cost ~2.6 s per 64 tokens; readahead = Turing's read-ahead, defaults (adaptive, 16 threads, blocking). Generations that hit end-of-text early are shorter than 64 tokens.
real_text_readahead_vs_mmap.finding: On real text read-ahead decodes at 6.2 tok/s (median of 12) against 4.7 for plain mmap (median of 8): about 1.3x. Real text left 9-18% of the chosen experts' bytes outside the page cache; bench's random ids 6-7%, where read-ahead was slower (decode_gpt_oss_120b). The adaptive switch (reads while >= 5% miss) is on in both regimes, so on this Mac the break-even lies between ~7% and ~12% missing: untuned.

findings: Qwen3-30B-A3B decodes real text at ~62 tok/s (median of 8, 44-69) with repack off; bench tg128 70.8 off, 45.3 on.

Inkling 2 Mini decodes real text at ~26 tok/s (median of 8, 23-26) with repack off; bench tg128 28.7. Output is coherent English (it reasons in plain text first: its template ignores enable_thinking).
Repack on was slower for Qwen3-30B-A3B on this Mac (bench tg 45.3 against 70.8) and swap use rose from 4.5 to 12 GB during it (the repacked copy is anonymous memory); not separated from the swapping.
Inkling 2 Mini with repack on aborts in llama.cpp at context creation: ggml-backend.cpp:1725 GGML_ASSERT(*cur_backend_id != -1) in llama_context::resolve_fused_ops (pin 171527522).

Turing bug found: TuringLlama::truncate ignores llama_memory_seq_rm's result. Inkling 2's memory is hybrid (grouped with Falcon-H1), whose suffix cannot be dropped, so prefill's prefix reuse (generate after eval, and turing serve's one-at-a-time path) fails with 'sequence positions must be consecutive'. Fixed after this run: truncate checks the result and clears the whole sequence when the suffix cannot be dropped, prefill re-evaluates what was cleared, and prompt-lookup drafts are off on recurrent and hybrid models (tests/test_llama_backend.py::test_prompt_reuse_on_recurrent_memory, a tiny Mamba). Checked on Inkling 2 Mini: two chat requests in a row through create_app, both 200, the second with 0 cached prompt tokens.
